basic_info.name: Mito Health
basic_info.category: At-cost DTC lab-testing marketplace + AI-powered preventive health / longevity membership platform (curated biomarker panels, imaging marketplace, AI concierge, clinician-reviewed action plans)
basic_info.country: United States (San Francisco HQ; lab testing available in all 50 states; founded 2023 in Singapore — first customers served through a Singapore clinic before US expansion)
basic_info.stage: Early-stage startup: founded 2023, Y Combinator S24 batch; $1.3M pre-seed (Apr 2023) + $2.2M seed (Mar 2025) = $4M total raised; no Series A announced as of Aug 2026 [uncertain: unannounced rounds possible]; small team (~5 per YC listing, likely stale)
basic_info.pricing_model: Optional membership at $9/month or $99/year (HSA/FSA eligible) on top of à-la-carte pay-as-you-go testing; members pay at-cost lab prices, non-members pay ~10% over at-cost. Advertised entry: 100+ biomarker panel from $349 one-time (Core); Duo bundle $680 for two people; individual panels from ~$89. Exact prices of Essential (107), Pro and Ultra (154) panels not consistently published [uncertain]. Consults $39 members / $99 non-members; supplements 30% off retail for members. Anti-margin stance: 'we profit from membership, not from your tests' — marketed example: same test $15 at Mito vs ~$50 bundled-subscription labs vs ~$89 direct-pay vs ~$300 hospital labs. No known price changes through Aug 2026 [uncertain].
basic_info.target_user: Health optimizers, biohackers and longevity-focused self-pay consumers in the US — especially cost-conscious ones shopping specific tests (Trustpilot use case: price-shopping an annual-exam test list vs expensive hospital/PCP labs); secondary: people priced out of Function/Superpower annual bundles who want flexible, one-off or à-la-carte testing.
basic_info.scale_metrics: Funding: $4M total — Y Combinator, Capital X, XA Network, Forge Ventures plus angels (Balaji Srinivasan, Nir Eyal, Kevin Aluwi/GoJek, Nas Daily, Prashanth Prakash/Accel, Alex Svanevik, Dhruv Arora/Syfe). Traction: ~1,000 users served via the original Singapore clinic (per YC profile, early figure); 'nearly doubled customer base' claim in 2025 Tatler Asia coverage; current member count, revenue and valuation all undisclosed [uncertain]. Own-cohort outcome stats: 64% discovered elevated health risks, 36% nutrient deficiencies, 4% critical conditions. Durability read: far sub-scale vs Function ($2.5B valuation) but cash-efficient and live in all 50 states; the durable asset is the at-cost marketplace positioning and advisor bench, not volume.

product.core_features: At-cost lab marketplace (1,000+ labs, scans and kits at member cost); curated panels — Mito Essential (107 biomarkers), Mito Core (125), Mito Pro, Mito Ultra (154); AI Concierge chat (build a custom panel, explain biomarkers, find cheapest lab); 60-second questionnaire with instant personalized test recommendations (including what to skip); clinician-reviewed results + personalized action plan; 1:1 virtual consults ($39 members / $99 non-members); upload of external lab reports (PDF/JPG/PNG under 10MB, not password-protected — team extracts biomarker data over a few days); health records vault with longitudinal tracking; proprietary biological age (LinAge2 algorithm, 29 health areas, shareable card); supplements at 30% off retail; whole-genome sequencing 30x (at-home saliva kit); at-home blood kits (Tasso device); partner network: Quest Diagnostics, Labcorp, BioReference, BodySpec (DEXA), Prenuvo (MRI); member early access to new diagnostics.
product.signature_differentiator: The anti-upsell economics: a lab marketplace that claims to profit when you test LESS — 'we profit from membership, not from your tests', with the AI Concierge explicitly recommending which tests to skip. Per-test price-comparison transparency across lab channels (marketed example: same test $15 at Mito vs ~$50 bundled-subscription labs vs ~$89 direct-pay labs vs ~$300 hospital labs) is a UX no one else leads with. Combined with marketplace breadth beyond blood (Prenuvo MRIs, BodySpec DEXA, 30x WGS, 1,000+ items) and a genuine geroscience advisory bench (Prof. Brian Kennedy, ex-Buck Institute CEO; Prof. Matt Kaeberlein), Mito positions as the transparent, low-cost, anti-Function alternative. Roadmap concept: 'AI care team lead' — AI as first-line touch with human clinician escalation.
product.lab_data_handling: Blood draws fulfilled by Quest, Labcorp and BioReference (CLIA-certified processing), order sent electronically and downloadable; one visit covers all tests. Cadence: annual testing at minimum with optional mid-year or targeted retests (no fixed 2x/year bundle — retests are à la carte). Imaging and advanced diagnostics via marketplace partners (BodySpec DEXA, Prenuvo preventive MRI), plus at-home Tasso kits and clinical-grade WGS 30x saliva kit. Ingestion of external results: manual upload of PDF/JPG/PNG (under 10MB, unprotected), extracted by the team into structured tracking over days. Turnaround: standard panels in 1-2 business days; specialty assays/kits longer. No CGM, no bundled wearable program.
product.family_dependents_depth: Thin — the only family surface is the Duo bundle ($680 for two people, partner framing). FAQ states each account is for one individual only: no dependent accounts, no caregiver mode, no pediatric reference ranges, no hereditary-risk linking across relatives, no shared family view. Mirrors the same structural gap as every US D2C lab player — a confirmed open lane for Dr. Exame.
product.doctor_sharing: Patient-mediated and basic: export the dashboard as a PDF and share via email, patient portal or print; original lab reports available in the Documents tab for the physician to review. Every order is reviewed and signed by a Mito-network physician (legal oversight, not a care relationship). Consults are explicitly 'health education, not medical advice'. No doctor portal, no structured consult brief, no SOAP export, no e-referral loop.
product.action_loop_monetization: Margin architecture inverts Function: labs sold at cost; revenue comes from the $9/month (or $99/year) membership, supplement commerce (30% off retail still leaves margin), $39 member consults, and non-members paying ~10% over at-cost prices. Post-interpretation loop = personalized action plans across supplements, exercise, nutrition and sleep, with year-round in-chat clinician escalation and AI coaching to keep members executing between tests. Supplement marketplace is the clearest action-loop commerce. No telemedicine, no prescriptions, no pharmacy. Claimed incentive alignment: 'profits when users make better decisions rather than buying more tests'.

technology.ai_approach: Consumer surface: Mito Concierge — an AI chat assistant that builds custom lab panels, explains what biomarkers mean, finds the cheapest lab, and coaches on acting on results; plus a 60-second questionnaire recommender producing instant test suggestions. Roadmap framing of an 'AI care team lead' (AI first-line, human escalation) announced with the seed round. Human-in-the-loop: every order signed by a network physician and every result clinician-reviewed before the analysis/action plan finalizes. Proprietary biological-age algorithm: LinAge2 covering 29 health areas (LinAge1 used for tests before Aug 1, 2025). No published model architecture, LLM vendor, benchmarks or validation studies.
technology.data_inputs: Blood biomarkers (107-154 depending on panel) via CLIA labs; member-uploaded external lab reports (PDF/JPG/PNG) extracted into structured data; whole-genome sequencing 30x; DEXA and MRI scan reports via partners; at-home kit results (Tasso); onboarding questionnaire and self-reported goals/health history. No wearable or CGM ingestion confirmed anywhere in product or FAQ [uncertain].
technology.data_interoperability: Ingestion: manual upload of external lab PDFs/JPGs/PNGs (under 10MB, not password-protected) with human-team extraction over days — no automated parsing claim. Exhaust: dashboard PDF export and downloadable original lab reports. No FHIR, no Apple Health Records, no Health Connect, no public API, no LIS integration, no WhatsApp-style channel documented — absence inferred from FAQ silence and product pages [uncertain]. Testing footprint US-only; data encrypted at rest and in transit; not shared with insurers or national databases; deletion via email request.
technology.platform: Web dashboard (desktop + mobile web) as the hub: quiz, catalog, booking, results, trends, biological age card, documents vault, Concierge chat, consult booking. No native iOS/Android app found on app stores in research [uncertain]; marketing via newsletter and Instagram.

ux.onboarding: Quiz-first commerce: answer a 60-second health questionnaire before paying anything and get an instant, personalized recommendation — which tests answer your question and which ones you can skip. Then book the best-price/convenient lab draw electronically. Time-to-value: standard panel results in 1-2 business days; the recommendation itself is immediate. This 'what NOT to test' onboarding is the most distinctive first-touch in the category.
ux.data_visualization: Dashboard with longitudinal trend tracking across test events, out-of-range flags, clinician-reviewed action plans, and a shareable biological-age card (LinAge2, 29 health areas) as the consumer-facing composite score. Community critique (r/MitoHealth): 'The analysis tells you what is out of range, but doesn't do a great job' at explaining what it means — members report being 'left with more questions than answers', pushing them toward the $39 consults.
ux.engagement_channel: Retention framed by the $9/month membership rather than an annual bundle: AI Concierge chat available year-round with in-chat clinician escalation, action-plan tracking between draws, email, and member early access to new diagnostics. Community: organic r/MitoHealth subreddit; brand presence via Instagram and longevity-culture events (Bryan Johnson 'Don't Die Summit' partnership, NYC Feb 2025 + Miami). No streaks, no gamification, no WhatsApp-equivalent channel.

trust_gaps.clinical_validation_trust: Strong structural hygiene: all processing in CLIA-certified labs (Quest/Labcorp/BioReference), every order signed by a Mito-network physician, every result clinician-reviewed before release, consults framed as 'health education, not medical advice'. Advisory/care bench: Prof. Brian Kennedy PhD (aging biology, 40+ years, former Buck Institute CEO), Prof. Matt Kaeberlein (biogerontology), Rhonda Collins FNP-C (care team lead, 15+ years), Dr. Ryan Ware MBBS. Cohort outcome stats are self-reported with no published methodology: 64% of members discovered elevated health risks, 36% nutrient deficiencies, 4% critical conditions needing immediate attention. No peer-reviewed validation of the AI layer or LinAge2. Trustpilot sentiment positive (price savings vs hospital labs, '3x the tests for less money', 'felt actually taken care of') but exact rating unverified [uncertain]. Counter-signal: an r/Function_Health thread describes upsell pressure ('trying to push thousands of dollars in additional tests') and Reddit users note shallow interpretation depth — both in tension with the anti-upsell positioning.
trust_gaps.regulatory_posture: Classic US cash-pay DTC lab wrapper: consumer-facing 'no doctor's order required' backed legally by network physicians signing every order; state-by-state physician-order compliance; CLIA-certified third-party processing (Mito itself is not a lab or medical provider). Consults deliberately scoped as education, not medical advice — keeps the AI layer outside FDA SaMD territory; no diagnosis claims; disclaimers on results. Privacy: encryption at rest/in transit, no insurer/national-database sharing, deletion on request; HIPAA specifics not published [uncertain]. HSA/FSA eligibility. No FDA device clearances claimed. No Brazil presence — no ANVISA RDC 657/2022 or LGPD exposure; for Dr. Exame, Mito's education-not-advice consult framing is the US analogue of the non-diagnosis compliance line.
trust_gaps.gaps_opportunities: What Mito does NOT do (Dr. Exame openings): (1) zero family depth — single-individual accounts, Duo bundle only, no dependents/caregiver/pediatric ranges/hereditary-risk view; (2) no doctor-facing workflow — PDF export only, no consult brief, no SOAP, no physician portal; (3) shallow interpretation — flags what's out of range, weak on 'what does it mean', monetizing the gap via $39 consults instead of closing it; (4) no native mobile app found; (5) no wearables/CGM/FHIR/Apple Health ingestion; (6) no automated PDF parsing (human extraction over days vs instant AI extraction); (7) US-only, English-only, no WhatsApp retention rail; (8) sub-scale traction and funding vs Function. What works (inspiration, not copy): at-cost transparency positioning ('profit from membership, not tests') as an anti-Function wedge; quiz-first onboarding with instant value and skip-recommendations that build trust; AI concierge as a curation gatekeeper over a 1,000+ item marketplace; $9/month low-friction membership decoupled from test pricing; imaging + WGS marketplace breadth; price-comparison UX per test; geroscience advisor bench for longevity credibility.
trust_gaps.relevance: High — the cleanest fast-follow of the Function model with an inverted-economics twist (at-cost marketplace + $9/mo membership vs prepaid $349-499 annual bundles). It validates the US playbook — 100+ biomarkers, AI concierge, clinician review, diagnostics marketplace — while its structural gaps (family/pediatric, doctor workflow, interpretation depth, Brazil/LGPD/WhatsApp) are exactly Dr. Exame's defensible pillars. No direct threat in Brazil; maximum value as a model to borrow positioning and onboarding mechanics from.
